newsitem.title: CANADA: Better jobs seen boosting Canadian consumer - bank.
newsitem.headline: Better jobs seen boosting Canadian consumer - bank.

text.p: An increase in the amount of full-time and higher-paying jobs are boosting Canadian consumer confidence and should continue doing so, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce economists said on Monday.

Bank economists said CIBC's Employment Quality Index, which tracks the quality of new jobs, showed improvement its measurment of employment stability, compensation and the proportion of full-time to part-time employment gains.
On a year-over-year basis the index rose by 3.6 percent in the second quarter of 1997.
"The combined impact of increased full-time jobs, job stability and compensation will help boost consumer spending in the second half of this year," said Tal.
CIBC said the compensation component of the index rose 4.1 percent, reflecting the increased proportion of jobs in high-paying industries such as manufacturing.
The employment stability portion of the index rose 3.8 percent in the second quarter, driven largely by a 3.9 percent rise in jobs in professional and managerial occupations.
CIBC economists said the full-time/part-time sub-index rose 0.1 percent, reversing a trend of declines in full-time employment versus part-time employment.
